name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican candidate holds a large fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price the GOP near 94%
Open seat removes incumbent effects but not the partisan baseline
model.rationale: This rural northwest Missouri seat leans heavily Republican, and no polling or expert ratings suggest a competitive race. Stigall has out-raised Smead roughly eight-to-one and markets price the Republican at about 94%, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending targeting the open seat would be the first sign the race is closer than the district's lean implies.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Missouri's sixth district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of about nineteen points toward the GOP. Longtime Representative Sam Graves is retiring, creating an open seat, but the underlying partisanship remains the dominant force in the race.

Republican Chris Stigall has raised nearly $600,000, far outpacing Democrat Josh Smead's roughly $72,000, and outside groups have spent modestly against Stigall. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 94% chance of holding the seat. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the race is rated Safe Republican, with the main question being the size of the winning margin rather than the outcome.
